title: Early PLA2R Status in Severe Anti-PLA2R-mediated Membranous Nephropathy and Long Term Kidney Outcome.
official: Early PLA2R Status in Severe Anti-PLA2R-mediated Membranous Nephropathy and Long Term Kidney Outcome.
summary:
This is a multicentric retrospective observational cohort study. The aim of this study is to evaluate, during the initial phase of immunosuppressive treatment for severe PLA2R-positive membranous nephropathy, the independent association between anti-PLA2R antibody trajectories and the occurrence of long-term major kidney events (within 10 years after treatment initiation).

The secondary objectives are :

To assess the association between the initial anti-PLA2R antibody trajectory (between 0 and 6 ± 3 months after treatment, before any potential re-treatment) and the occurrence of nephrological remission.

To assess the association between the initial anti-PLA2R antibody trajectory (between 0 and 6 ± 3 months after treatment, before any potential re-treatment) and the occurrence of immunological remission.

To evaluate, in real-world practice, the safety of immunosuppressive therapies in the treatment of severe PLA2R-positive membranous nephropathy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient followed in 8 nephrology departments of AP-HP between 01/01/2017 and 12/31/2026
* Age \> 6 years
* With serodiagnosis of MN via identification of anti-PLA2R antibodies
* Treatment with an immunosuppressive drug.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of MN without testing for anti-PLA2R antibodies
* Refusal to use the data
* Occurrence of the primary endpoint at the time of disease diagnosis (diagnosis of membranous nephropathy at the stage of end-stage kidney disease)
* Lack of patient follow-up at the centers participating in the study
* Lack of reassessment of anti-PLA2R antibody titers within 12 months after initiation of immunosuppressive therapy
